- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.7) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes or volatility — model tends to overcorrect downward; add 1–2% buffer to prevent premature drop.
- Lagged sentiment effects: if sentiment rises sharply 3–5 days before forecast horizon, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to account for delayed market reaction.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model forecasts a sharp rise after a spike, cap the next 3–5 days’ forecast at 10–15% below peak to avoid over-optimism.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early in cycle — reduce first 5–7 days by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.
- Sentiment decay: if sentiment drops below 0.5 over 3+ days, reduce forecast slope downward by 0.2–0.5% per day to reflect cooling momentum.
